f_Sun_0: Sun. The Sun is a star! About 1.3 million Earths could fit inside it.
f_Sun_1: Sun. The Sun spins around once in about 25 days.
f_Mercury_0: Mercury. Mercury is the closest planet to the Sun.
f_Mercury_1: Mercury. Mercury goes all the way around the Sun in just 88 days.
f_Venus_0: Venus. A day on Venus is longer than its whole year!
f_Earth_1: Earth. Earth goes around the Sun once every year. That is 365 days.
f_Mars_0: Mars. Mars looks red because of rusty dust.
f_Mars_1: Mars. Mars has two small moons.
f_Mars_2: Mars. A day on Mars is a little longer than a day on Earth.
f_Jupiter_0: Jupiter. Jupiter is the biggest planet. About 1,300 Earths could fit inside!
f_Jupiter_1: Jupiter. A day on Jupiter is only about 10 hours.
f_Uranus_0: Uranus. Uranus spins tipped over on its side.
f_Uranus_1: Uranus. Uranus takes 84 years to go around the Sun.
f_Neptune_0: Neptune. Neptune is the farthest planet from the Sun.
f_Neptune_1: Neptune. Neptune takes about 165 years to go around the Sun.
